raw_response:
I farm the same 10.1 mu in wheat and maize, same as these past years. For me, the main thing is not to make fancy changes, it is to keep the land steady and make sure the family still has income. Wheat and maize together are the safest here. If one side goes bad, maybe the other side still gives something. I do not read books, so I look at what worked before, what my neighbors do, and how the field looked last year. Last year fertilizer helped the wheat fill better, so I will not cut too much. But money is still tight because some people in the house work outside and cash must be kept for living too. I will do what is common here: wheat in October with base fertilizer, then one topdress later if the crop looks like it needs it; after wheat harvest I plant maize right away, no delay, because that turnaround is very short. I have well water, but pumping costs money, so I only irrigate at the important times, not too many times.
